memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Pharaoh and all his officials and all the Egyptians got up during the night,
and there was loud wailing in Egypt, for there was not a house without someone
dead." - Ex 12:30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse is simply grief, and Scripture records it plainly. There was not a
house without someone dead.

We should not read this coldly. God takes no pleasure in it either. Ezekiel
33:11 records Him saying, "I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but
rather that they turn from their ways and live."

It is worth asking how it came to this. Pharaoh was warned before every single
plague. He was given opportunity after opportunity. Each time he promised and
then went back on his word once the pressure lifted. Exodus tells us both that
Pharaoh hardened his own heart and that God hardened it. Scripture holds those
together without apology, and believers have long differed on precisely how they
fit. What is clear is that Pharaoh was never a victim. He chose this, again and
again, and a whole nation paid the price of one man's stubbornness.

Leaders bear weight. When a person in authority hardens themselves against God,
others suffer for it. That should make us pray for those who lead us, in
government, at work, in our churches, and in our homes (1 Tim 2:1-2).

And it should make us examine our own hearts before they set.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an area where you have promised God something under pressure and
   gone back on it afterwards?
2. Who are you responsible for, and how is your walk with God affecting them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, guard my heart from hardening. Where I have made promises to You and
broken them, forgive me and make me steady. Amen.
